name: Question 5
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14067574/assets/85b4da8c0fa35867871b6254ba20f505b7596f2c97226adb2ed01339fe4cbedf.png)

Calculate the flux of the vector field $F(x,y)=5{e}^{-x}\,i+4\,j$ through the curve $C$ given by $r(t)=\operatorname{ln}⁡t\,i+t\,j$ for $t\in [1,e],$ measured with respect to the unit normal vector $n$ on $C,$ as shown above.
worked_solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field and $C$ is a piecewise-smooth, simple curve, then the flux of $F$ across $C$ measured with respect to a unit normal vector $n$ on $C$ is given by

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={\int }_{C}P\,\text{d}y-Q\,\text{d}x.
$$

To apply this formula, 

- the curve should be parameterized as $r(t)$ for $t\in [a,b],$ and

- the unit normal vector $n$ *must* be a ${90}^{∘}$ clockwise rotation of the unit tangent vector $T(t).$

In this case, $n$ is indeed a ${90}^{∘}$ clockwise rotation of $T,$ so we can apply the above formula. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14067574/assets/559bbc20aa7d47eaad47a8975f80c8efb91bd03bc816357bc6047675dc755c9b.png)

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,y=t.
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(x,y) & =5{e}^{-x}=5{e}^{-\operatorname{ln}⁡t}=\frac{5}{t}, \\ Q(x,y) & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x(t)$ and $y(t)$ along the curve, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t)=\frac{1}{t}, \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{C}P\,\text{d}y-Q\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}(P\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}-Q\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}(\frac{5}{t})\cdot (1)-(4)\cdot (\frac{1}{t})\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{1}{t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡t{|}_{1}^{e} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Calculate the flux of the vector field F(x,y)=5e−xi+4j through the curve C given by r(t)=ln⁡ti+tj for t∈[1,e], measured with respect to the unit normal vector n on C, as shown above.

a
 −1
b
 −2
c
 2
d
 1
e
 0
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

If F=Pi+Qj is a vector field and C is a piecewise-smooth, simple curve, then the flux of F across C measured with respect to a unit normal vector n on C is given by ∫CF⋅nds=∫CPdy−Qdx. To apply this formula,

  • the curve should be parameterized as r(t) for t∈[a,b], and

  • the unit normal vector n must be a 90∘ clockwise rotation of the unit tangent vector T(t).

In this case, n is indeed a 90∘ clockwise rotation of T, so we can apply the above formula.

Along the curve C, we have x=ln⁡t,y=t.

Therefore,

P(x,y)=5e−x=5e−ln⁡t=5t,Q(x,y)=4.

Computing the derivatives of x(t) and y(t) along the curve, we get

dxdt=ddt(ln⁡t)=1t,dydt=ddt(t)=1.

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

∫CF⋅nds=∫CPdy−Qdx=∫1e(P⋅dydt−Q⋅dxdt)dt=∫1e(5t)⋅(1)−(4)⋅(1t)dt=∫1e1tdt=ln⁡t|1e=1
